description: Rebuild admin page builder editor (resources/views/admin/page-builder/edit.blade.php) into a WordPress-like two-panel UI with SortableJS drag-drop (CDN), Alpine.js component state management, per-type inline editing forms, and AJAX auto-save. The existing save route (POST admin/pages/{page}/builder/save, named admin.page-builder.save) accepts components[] array and is kept unchanged.
steps: Load SortableJS from CDN in the edit.blade.php @section('scripts'): `<script src='https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/sortablejs@1.15.6/Sortable.min.js'></script>`. This is the only new dependency. Do NOT add it to package.json.

Replace the entire content of resources/views/admin/page-builder/edit.blade.php with a new two-panel layout using Alpine.js x-data for state management. The top-level Alpine component `pageBuilder` holds: `components` (array, initialized from PHP-rendered JSON of existing components), `saving` (bool), `lastSaved` (string), `addComponent(type)`, `removeComponent(index)`, `toggleVisibility(index)`, `editingIndex` (int or null), `saveAll()` async method.

Left panel (lg:col-span-8): Header row with page title + breadcrumb. Canvas area: a `<div id='sortable-canvas'>` containing one card per component. Each card shows: drag handle (≡ icon), component type badge, preview of first content field (truncated 50 chars), visibility toggle (eye icon Alpine x-model), edit button, delete button. Below the edit button, an inline accordion (x-show='editingIndex === index') renders the per-type form fields (see step 5).

Right panel (lg:col-span-4): Sticky card with section 'Add Component' listing all 15 component types as buttons (emoji icon + name + category badge). Clicking a type calls addComponent(type) which pushes a new component object with default content into the components array and sets editingIndex to the new index. Below the picker: 'Save All' button that calls saveAll(), shows saving spinner, displays last-saved timestamp. Also show page status (published/draft), slug, and link to preview.

Implement per-type inline form fields as a Blade @switch block inside the accordion. Each case renders labeled inputs/textareas that use `x-model='components[editingIndex].content.fieldname'` (Alpine.js). Forms use nested object binding. For repeating items (features list, testimonials, pricing plans, team members, gallery images, FAQ, social links), use `x-for` loops with add/remove row buttons. Default content values for each type: hero={title:'Hero Section',subtitle:'Tagline here',button_text:'Mulai Sekarang',button_link:'#',badge:'',height:'large',text_align:'center'}; text={heading:'',text:'',text_align:'left',max_width:'medium'}; features={heading:'Fitur Unggulan',description:'',columns:3,features:[{icon:'⚡',title:'Fitur 1',description:'Deskripsi'}]}; cta={heading:'Siap Bergabung?',text:'Daftar sekarang dan rasakan manfaatnya.',button_text:'Mulai Sekarang',button_link:'/kontak',style:'gradient'}; testimonials={heading:'Testimoni',columns:3,testimonials:[{name:'',position:'',text:'',rating:5,photo:''}]}; pricing={heading:'Harga',plans:[{name:'',description:'',price:'0',currency:'Rp',period:'bulan',featured:false,button_text:'Pilih',button_link:'#',features:['']}]}; team={heading:'Tim Kami',columns:4,members:[{name:'',position:'',bio:'',photo:''}]}; gallery={heading:'Galeri',columns:3,layout:'grid',images:[{url:'',alt:'',caption:''}]}; faq={heading:'FAQ',faqs:[{question:'',answer:''}]}; contact-form={title:'Hubungi Kami',subtitle:'',button_text:'Kirim Pesan',show_city:false,show_subject:false}; video={heading:'',url:'',caption:''}; map={heading:'Lokasi',embed_url:'',address:'',directions_url:''}; social={heading:'Ikuti Kami',links:[{platform:'instagram',url:''}]}; newsletter={heading:'Newsletter',subtitle:'',placeholder:'Email Anda',button_text:'Berlangganan'}; html={html:'<!-- Tulis HTML Anda di sini -->'}.

Implement saveAll() as an Alpine.js method: builds the POST body as JSON with `components` array (each item: component_type, content, settings, sort_order from array index, is_visible). Uses fetch() with method POST, Content-Type application/json, X-CSRF-TOKEN header (from meta tag). On success shows toast via window.showToast (already defined in admin.js). On error shows error toast. Updates lastSaved timestamp.

Initialize SortableJS after the DOM is ready using Alpine.js `x-init` or a `@script` block. `new Sortable(document.getElementById('sortable-canvas'), { handle: '.drag-handle', animation: 150, onEnd(evt) { const comp = pageBuilder.components.splice(evt.oldIndex, 1)[0]; pageBuilder.components.splice(evt.newIndex, 0, comp); } })`. Note: `pageBuilder` must be accessible from the Sortable callback — use Alpine.store or pass it via closure.

Auto-save: Set an interval in the x-init that calls saveAll() every 60 seconds if `components.length > 0`. Also call saveAll() when Alpine detects `components` change using a debounced `$watch('components', ...)` (500ms debounce). This mirrors WordPress auto-draft behavior.
Add a 'Preview' button in the header row that opens `{{ route('admin.page-builder.preview', $page) }}` in a new tab.
Ensure the form gracefully handles the case where $page->components is empty (new page builder page) — initialize components array as `[]` in that case.

The Blade template renders initial component data using: `x-data="pageBuilder({{ json_encode($page->components->map(fn($c) => ['id' => $c->id, 'component_type' => $c->component_type, 'content' => $c->content, 'settings' => $c->settings ?? [], 'sort_order' => $c->sort_order, 'is_visible' => $c->is_visible])->values()->toJson() }})"`. Define `pageBuilder(initialComponents)` as a global JS function (in a @push('scripts') block) that returns the Alpine component object.

Style notes: Canvas cards use bg-white rounded-xl border border-slate-200 shadow-sm hover:shadow-md transition-shadow. Drag handle (.drag-handle) uses cursor-grab text-slate-400. Component type badge uses colored variants (hero=purple, text=blue, features=green, cta=orange, etc.) for quick visual identification. Right panel is `sticky top-6`. The two-panel grid: `class='grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-12 gap-6'` with left=lg:col-span-8 and right=lg:col-span-4`.
acceptance_criteria: Visiting /admin/pages/{id}/builder shows a two-panel layout: canvas (left) + component picker (right)
Clicking any component type in the right panel appends a new component card to the canvas
Clicking Edit on a card expands an inline form with pre-filled fields for that component type
Dragging and dropping cards reorders them (SortableJS working)
Clicking Save All posts to admin.page-builder.save route and shows success toast
Reloading the page shows previously saved components in their saved order
Visibility toggle (eye icon) toggles is_visible on the component object
Auto-save triggers every 60 seconds if components exist
npm run build succeeds (no new npm packages added)
verification: npm run build (must complete without errors)
Navigate to /admin/pages/{id}/builder where {id} is a page with use_page_builder=true
Add a hero component, fill in title and subtitle fields, click Save All
Reload page — confirm hero component appears with the saved values
Add a features component, drag it above hero, save, reload — confirm new order
Visit frontend page URL — confirm hero and features components render on the page
